title: Action needed to tackle Jersey's 'biodiversity crisis'
summary:
A scrutiny panel has heard Jersey is in a "biodiversity crisis", amid concerns the government is not focusing on the environment enough.
Willie Peggie, government Director of Natural Environment, said the Environment Department needed time and resources for a state of nature report.
Piers Sangan, who runs Sangan Island Conversation, said a biodiversity crisis included more invasive species, fewer native species, and a decline in the ecosystem.
The environment minister said policies were being worked on to further protect the environment.
Peggie said any state of nature report should be similar to those in the UK, external, Guernsey, external and Alderney, external.

title: This California Wind Farm Is Having A Topsy-Turvy Effect On Local Weather
summary:
Fewer than two hours from the heart of Los Angeles, there is a wind farm.
Here, at San Gorgonio Pass, over 600 turbines generate enough electricity to power thousands of homes.
In fact, this wind farm alone is estimated to prevent the release of nearly 1 million tons of carbon dioxide every single year.
What's interesting about it, though, is that the San Gorgonio Wind Farm is changing the local climate ... just not in the way you might expect.
In 1989, meteorologists visited San Gorgonio and performed the first ever field campaign in an operational wind farm.

title: Greenpeace drops boulders in North Sea fishing grounds off Norfolk
summary:
Greenpeace has dropped nine boulders off the east coast of England to create a barrier that disrupts bottom trawling by fishing vessels.
The environmental campaigners' ship Arctic Sunrise released the rocks, without a licence, over the weekend about 50km (30 miles) east of Great Yarmouth, Norfolk.
Greenpeace claimed it had "effectively closed 116 sq km (45 sq miles) of the Southern North Sea Marine Protected Area (MPA) to bottom trawling".
When asked if it had permission to drop the boulders, Greenpeace said this was a "last resort" for it, and it did not have a licence.
It said that after years of meeting with politicians and the government to try to protect marine protected areas, progress had been "at a glacial pace".

title: The polar vortex is about to go haywire
summary:
Something “unprecedented” is happening in the atmosphere: the Arctic polar vortex, a spinning mass of air high above the North Pole, is collapsing.
Waves in the atmosphere known as “Rossby waves” can cause the polar vortex to wobble and weaken.
During a big polar vortex disruption—what scientists call a “sudden stratospheric warming”—the vortex can drift, stretch, split into multiple swirls or change direction.
Polar vortex disruptions normally occur deep into the winter, Cohen says, so a sudden stratospheric warming in November is unusual.
“Where everything sets up is still in question.”Not all polar vortex disruptions look the same.
